newsitem.title: GERMANY: Milder conditions will help German winter crops.
newsitem.headline: Milder conditions will help German winter crops.

text.p: A slight let-up in the big freeze covering Europe is helping German winter rapeseed and barley to escape serious winter kill, an official at the meteorological institute (DWD) said.
"The worst may be over, but temperatures are not yet back above zero and there are still cold air masses in the east that will prevent an early thaw," he said.
DWD in a weekly report forecast maximum day temperatures around minus three degress and light night frosts in the period to Jan 15.
It recorded daytime temperatures between minus one to minus seven and night frosts between minus 10 and minus 20 in the Jan 2-8 period.
This caused some damage to rapeseed and barley crops under insufficient snow cover and harmed some winter wheat in eastern Germany.
But frosts also hardened the crops against pest damage in the spring.
Livestock farmers reported problems with frozen pipes and frost in feed silos.
Compound feed manufacturers were asking for surcharges of 5.00-9.00 marks per tonne of beef feed and 2.50-5.00 marks per tonne of pig and poultry feed to offset higher transport costs, traders said.
Many canals are frozen and road or rail transport space is limited and expensive.
